citation.title: FAIR-MAST: A fusion device data management system
citation.authors: Jackson S, Khan S, Cummings N, Hodson J, de Witt S, Pamela S, Akers R, Thiyagalingam J, The MAST Team

topic: FAIR data management for historical MAST diagnostic data. It combines a PostgreSQL metadata index, S3/Ceph Zarr object storage and REST/GraphQL APIs.
own_question: How can archived MAST diagnostic data be made findable, remotely accessible and ready for AI/ML analysis?
actual_method_and_evidence: This is a software description. Its only empirical test is a transfer benchmark of 100 camera images, about 17 GB, run on an internal UKAEA cluster. The paper reports about 83 MB/s and 2 s latency for the new system, compared with 7.4 MB/s and 23 s for UDA. It contains no CES, KSTAR, ion-temperature or nowcasting content.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. The latency figures refer to offline archive retrieval, not to real-time diagnostic report arrival.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable. There is no model validation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite this paper as evidence for real-time or online data availability.
Do not equate its archive retrieval latency with CES report latency or our 10 ms computation.
Do not imply it addresses KSTAR, CES or impurity ion temperature.
Do not cite it as evidence that ML on fusion data improves prediction.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The source concerns offline data infrastructure for a different device, so it has no bearing on the causal CES nowcasting question. At most it could support an optional data-availability remark, but it is not needed.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
